title: High-touch Intake Accelerator and First-Look Scoring
creator: Lena Ortiz
description:
Summary:
Create a repeatable, lightweight intake accelerator for high-touch (sales/CS) enterprise feature requests that gives PMs a structured first-look score and an initial scoping packet within 72 hours. The intent is to reduce friction for Sales/CS, standardize handoffs, and surface economic and technical risk signals earlier.

Background and problem:
Sales and CS teams receive complex enterprise asks that are inconsistent in completeness. PMs spend multiple back-and-forths to gather required context before an initial prioritization decision; this delays discovery and causes lost momentum for proof-of-concepts. Existing intake playbooks are either too heavyweight (full PRD) or too generic (one-line requests). We need a pragmatic middle path: a 72-hour "first-look" output with a numerical score and recommended next steps (POC, design spike, roadmap candidate, or no-go).

Scope:
- Design a one-page intake form for Sales/CS (auto-populated fields where possible).
- Implement a scoring rubric (value, technical risk, regulatory friction, revenue proximity, implementation effort).
- Build a template first-look packet (summary, score, top unknowns, initial cost/effort band, recommended next step).
- Run a pilot with three strategic accounts and the sales engineers team.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for full PRD or engineering discovery.
- Not intended for low-touch self-serve feature requests.

Deliverables:
1) Intake form + Slack/Sheets + instructions for Sales/CS.
2) Scoring rubric and calculator (spreadsheet + simple UI mock in Figma).
3) First-look packet template and GitHub template for follow-ups.
4) Pilot run results and adoption playbook.

Success metrics:
- Median time from Sales ask -> PM first-look <= 72 hours (target: 48 hours).
- Reduction in back-and-forths to gather basic specs by 60% during pilot.
- Pilot feedback: 8/10 or higher from Sales/CS on clarity/usefulness.

Constraints and assumptions:
- We can instrument a simple Google Form + Sheets to start (no backend needed).
- Engineering bandwidth for any prototype work limited until Q1 2026.
- Must align with current enterprise security requirements; no sensitive PII in intake forms.

Stakeholders and reviewers:
- Sales: Maya Chen (AE lead)
- CS: Tomas Rivera (Director CS)
- Eng: Priya Nair (Runtime lead), Ben Gallagher (Platform)
- Legal/Compliance: Nora Kim

Acceptance criteria (see separate field):

Notes on prioritization rationale:
We prioritize high-touch intake because these requests have the largest revenue and product-shaping impact. Shortening first-response time will increase conversion of proposals to paid pilots and improve product-market signals for roadmap decisions.
acceptance_criteria: Intake form prototype exists and is validated with at least 5 AEs/CS reps
Scoring rubric documented, with example completed scores for 3 historical asks
First-look packet template created and populated for 3 pilot requests
Pilot kickoff scheduled and at least one pilot completed with documented feedback
SLA measurement in place (time-to-first-look) and dashboard created
notes: Prefer starting with a Google Form + Zapier -> Sheets flow to minimize infra work.
Discussed auto-populating account details via CRM integration; defer to follow-up spike (estimate 3 pts).
PM will own training materials; Sales Ops will own rollout communications.
Consider a lightweight webhook from form to a private channel so PMs see requests in realtime.
